item.research_question: What are the advances in design, synthesis, and applications of high-entropy metal-organic frameworks (HE-MOFs) for catalysis and energy storage?
item.processing_route: Various methods, including solvothermal, hydrothermal, co-precipitation, mechanochemical synthesis, and electrodeposition
key_findings: HE-MOFs have abundant active sites, stable framework structures, and adjustable chemical properties
HE-MOFs demonstrate exceptional catalytic activity and impressive electrochemical energy storage performance
The high-entropy strategy can improve the catalytic activity and stability of MOFs
HE-MOFs have potential applications in various fields, including catalysis, energy storage, and conversion
item.mechanism: The high-entropy strategy can create lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion, and a cocktail effect, which contribute to the attractive properties of HE-MOFs
item.limitations: The current reports on the application of HE-MOFs in catalysis are limited, and more systematic studies are needed to explore the mechanism of how the high-entropy strategy enhances catalytic activity
item.future_work: Further research is needed to design advanced HE-MOFs with desired properties and to explore their potential applications in various fields
quotes: HE-MOFs have garnered significant attention in the fields of catalysis and renewable energy technology
The high-entropy strategy has progressively extended to a broader range of material systems
HE-MOFs possess three unique effects, including lattice distortion, sluggish diffusion, and cocktail effect

item.research_question: How do high-entropy metal-organic frameworks (HE-MOFs) perform in energy storage applications?
item.material_system: Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn-based Na1.19(Zn0.23Mn0.19Ni0.19Cu0.21Co0.18)[Fe(CN)6]0.81□0.19 (M5HCF), HE-PBA, HEO850
key_findings: Average capacity of 75 mAh g−1 at 0.5 C
Capacity retention of 87% after 1000 cycles at 1 C
Specific capacity of 570.9 mAh g−1 after 200 cycles at 0.1 C
Ultra-stable cycling performance with a negligible capacity decay of 0.043% per cycle at 0.5 C after 800 cycles
Specific capacitance of 175 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1
Specific capacitance of 336 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1
item.mechanism: The high-entropy strategy enables M5HCF to possess a smaller bandgap, reducing the difficulty associated with electron excitation and leading to faster diffusion kinetics
item.limitations: The development of HE-MOFs is in its nascent stages, and there is still much research work that needs to be performed to achieve further progress in this field
item.future_work: Research on high-entropy MOFs containing six or more metal components is necessary to explore the influence of increased configurational entropy on alleviating the Jahn-Teller effect
quotes: applying the high-entropy strategy to HE-MOFs introduces multiple metal ions into their framework structure, creating abundant redox-active sites and thereby enhancing their electrochemical performance
the high-entropy strategy enables M5HCF to possess a smaller bandgap than its different quaternary counterparts (M4HCF)

records.text: Paper card. Question: How do high-entropy metal-organic frameworks (HE-MOFs) perform in energy storage applications?. System: Mn, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn-based Na1.19(Zn0.23Mn0.19Ni0.19Cu0.21Co0.18)[Fe(CN)6]0.81□0.19 (M5HCF), HE-PBA, HEO850. Test conditions: 0.5 C, 1 C, 0.1 C, 0.2 C, 0.5 C, 1 C, -10 to 80 °C. Findings: Average capacity of 75 mAh g−1 at 0.5 C; Capacity retention of 87% after 1000 cycles at 1 C; Specific capacity of 570.9 mAh g−1 after 200 cycles at 0.1 C; Ultra-stable cycling performance with a negligible capacity decay of 0.043% per cycle at 0.5 C after 800 cycles; Specific capacitance of 175 F g−1 at 5 mV s−1; Specific capacitance of 336 F g−1 at a current density of 1 A g−1. Mechanism: The high-entropy strategy enables M5HCF to possess a smaller bandgap, reducing the difficulty associated with electron excitation and leading to faster diffusion kinetics. Limitations: The development of HE-MOFs is in its nascent stages, and there is still much research work that needs to be performed to achieve further progress in this field. Future work: Research on high-entropy MOFs containing six or more metal components is necessary to explore the influence of increased configurational entropy on alleviating the Jahn-Teller effect. Quote: "applying the high-entropy strategy to HE-MOFs introduces multiple metal ions into their framework structure, creating abundant redox-active sites and thereby enhancing their electrochemical performance"
